「帽子、取った！
　ぼっとしてるから、とられるんだ！」
lines.english: “Your cap! I took it! That's what you get for standing around daydreaming!”

lines.japanese: 「返して欲しいか！」
lines.english: “Want it back?”

lines.japanese: どうでも良かった。
lines.english: It did not matter.

lines.japanese:
備品の管理など微々たることだ。
　損害にも打撃にもならない。
lines.english: Keeping track of one minor piece of issued equipment was trivial. Its loss would neither harm nor hinder him.

lines.japanese:
あずさの行為はまるっきり無駄であり、究極的に
愚かであったため、忍はそこに人間心理における整
合性を見いだすことができないでいた。
lines.english: Azusa's act was so utterly pointless, so supremely foolish, that Shinobu could make no sense of it as human behavior.

lines.japanese: 幼稚な言動。
lines.english: Childish words and actions.

lines.japanese:
今の紅緒あずさには価値がない。
　ただ未熟なものでしかない。
lines.english: Azusa Benio, as she was now, had no value. She was simply immature.

lines.japanese: （だけど……）
lines.english: (And yet…)

lines.japanese: 「返して欲しかったら……欲しかったら」
lines.english: “If you want it back… if you want it…”

lines.japanese:
泣きそうな顔。
　幼い忍の心中、急速に低下する驚異度。
lines.english: Her face was on the verge of tears. In young Shinobu's mind, her threat level plummeted.

lines.japanese: 「返して、欲しかったら―――」
lines.english: “If you want it back—”

lines.japanese: （あまりにも圧倒的な、それは）
lines.english: (It was so utterly overwhelming—)

lines.japanese:
消え入りそうな、種火。
　意味はない。
lines.english: A pilot flame, ready to gutter out. It meant nothing.

lines.japanese:
だが罪もない。
　死ぬこともない。
lines.english: But it was innocent too. Nor did it need to die.

lines.japanese: 「……あげる」
lines.english: “…You can have it.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「欲しいんなら、あげる」
lines.english: “If you want it, you can have it.”

lines.japanese: 背を向ける。
lines.english: He turned his back.

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと！！」
lines.english: “H-hey! Wait!”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ……逃げるの……？」
lines.english: “What… you’re running away…?”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 歩み去る忍のあとに、あずさがついてくる。
lines.english: Azusa followed in Shinobu's wake as he walked away.

lines.japanese: （まずいな、ついてこられると）
lines.english: (This is bad. If she follows me…)

lines.japanese:
つきまとわれることが一番困る。
　個人情報の漏洩経路は少ない方がいい。
lines.english: Being followed would be the worst possible outcome. The fewer channels through which personal information might leak, the better.

lines.japanese:
忍はその件で特に指示を受けてはいないが、警戒
はしておくべきだ。
lines.english: Shinobu had received no specific instructions on the matter, but caution was warranted.

lines.japanese: 組織の一員として―――
lines.english: As a member of the organization—

lines.japanese: （いや、それはないか……平気だ）
lines.english: (No, that won't happen… It'll be all right.)

lines.japanese:
本気で心配しかかった時、スイッチが入ったよう
に感覚が開けた。
lines.english: Just as he began to worry in earnest, his senses opened as if a switch had been thrown.

lines.japanese: そして、
lines.english: And then,

lines.japanese:
（あずさは僕に帽子を返してくる……
　そして立ち去る……だから平気―――）
lines.english: (Azusa is going to give back my cap… Then she'll leave… so it'll be all right—)

lines.japanese: （このまま歩いていけばいい）
lines.english: (All I have to do is keep walking.)

lines.japanese: （危険は、感じられない）
lines.english: (I sense no danger.)

lines.japanese:
直感はほとんど映像化されていた。
　いつでも見えるわけではない。
lines.english: His intuition had almost become an image. It was not something he could always see.

lines.japanese:
時折、未来の出来事が脳内に収束して、光景を再
現するのである。
lines.english: At times, a future event would converge inside his mind and reconstitute itself as a scene.

lines.japanese: PRECOGNITION―――
lines.english: PRECOGNITION—

lines.japanese:
未来視と呼ばれる力。
　存在する可能性が理論値としては予測されながら
も、有する者のいない力。
lines.english: The power known as foresight. Its possible existence had been predicted in theory, but no one possessed it.

lines.japanese: 神の領域に属する能力。
lines.english: A faculty belonging to the realm of God.
“…I'll give it back.”

lines.japanese: 果たして、幻視は現視となった。
lines.english: And sure enough, the vision became actual sight.

lines.japanese: （予知に現実が、追いついてくる……）
lines.english: (Reality is catching up with the precognition…)

lines.japanese: あずさは忍の頭上に帽子を叩きつけるように乗せた。
lines.english: Azusa jammed the cap back down onto Shinobu's head.

lines.japanese: 「……ばーか」
lines.english: “…Idiot.”

lines.japanese: とだけ告げると、反対側に走り去っていく。
lines.english: Having said only that, she ran off in the opposite direction.

lines.japanese: （それでいい……僕に関わると、不幸になる）
lines.english: (That's how it should be… Getting involved with me will only make her miserable.)

lines.japanese: また未来視。
lines.english: Another vision of the future.

lines.japanese: 連続して起こるのは珍しい。
lines.english: It was rare for them to come in succession.

lines.japanese:
みじかな映像。
　だがそれは決定的に結末を示唆している。
lines.english: A brief image. Yet it gave a decisive indication of how things would end.

lines.japanese: 紅緒あずさ。
lines.english: Azusa Benio.

lines.japanese:
どうでも良い存在である。
　仮に何らかの事情で死亡したとしても、忍が心痛
めることはない。
lines.english: She was of no consequence. Even if circumstances led to her death, Shinobu's heart would not ache.

lines.japanese: 冷徹な意志を揺るがすものではない。
lines.english: It would not shake his cold resolve.

lines.japanese:
任務・組織に対する帰属意識は強い。いや……幼い
忍の世界全てといって良かった。
lines.english: His loyalty to his mission and the organization ran deep. No… to the young Shinobu, they were the entire world.

lines.japanese: （だからこれでいい……そう思っていたはずなのに）
lines.english: (So this is for the best… I should have believed that.)

lines.japanese: なのに。
lines.english: And yet.

lines.japanese:
あの日、少年たちに暴行を受けていた少女の、悲痛
な叫びが意識から離れない。
lines.english: The anguished cry of the girl the boys had assaulted that day would not leave his mind.

lines.japanese:
忍の発案による。
　当初は単純に拾った家具等を置いただけの、秘密基地のような場所だった。
　工場が本格的なくつろぎ空間へと変化したのは、忍がおやつを備蓄しはじめて
からだ。
　何事も凝る性分である樋口章二が、固形燃料などのキャンプ道具を調達してく
ると、さらに空間は強固になっていく。
　聖域としての強度を、持ちはじめたのである。
lines.english: It was Shinobu's idea. At first, it was no more than a secret hideout, furnished with whatever odds and ends they'd picked up. The factory only became a real place to relax once Shinobu began stockpiling snacks there. Then Shouji Higuchi, constitutionally incapable of doing anything by halves, procured camping gear such as solid fuel, and the space grew sturdier still. It began to acquire the strength of a sanctuary.

lines.japanese: 現在の備蓄量は以下の通りである。
lines.english: Their current provisions were as follows.

lines.japanese:
・乾燥野菜スープ（４食）
　・固形チーズ（１食）
　・ビスケット（１袋）
　・乾パン（６缶）
　・ミネストローネスープ（３食）
　・ピラフ缶（２缶）
　・袋めん（５食）
　・乾燥野菜（４食）
　・飴（２袋）
　・チョコレート（１枚）
lines.english:
• Dehydrated vegetable soup (4 servings)
• Hard cheese (1 serving)
• Biscuits (1 package)
• Hardtack (6 cans)
• Minestrone (3 servings)
• Canned pilaf (2 cans)
• Instant noodles (5 servings)
• Dehydrated vegetables (4 servings)
• Candy (2 bags)
• Chocolate (1 bar)

lines.japanese:
戦争終結後、社会の混乱と空洞化によって、新規の娯楽放送はほとんど放映さ
れていない。
　特にテレビ放送局は絶命状態である。
　ラジオなども再放送を延々と流す他、目新しいものは収録されてはいない。
lines.english: Since the war ended, the upheaval and hollowing-out of society have all but driven new entertainment from the airwaves. Television stations in particular are effectively dead. Radio fares little better: aside from endless reruns, nothing new is being recorded.

lines.japanese:
しかし政府広報などはラジオなどを通じて行われている。
　また一部の有志によって、イマジナリー・ネットなどを用いた自主的な情報伝
達経路が確立されつつある。
lines.english: Government bulletins, however, are still broadcast over the radio and similar channels. Meanwhile, volunteers are beginning to establish independent channels of communication through the Imaginary Net and similar systems.

lines.japanese:
非ステロイド性消炎鎮痛剤を主剤とした市販の鎮痛剤。
　効能は頭痛・歯痛・生理痛・筋肉痛・関節痛・腰痛・打撲、骨折による痛み・
外傷による痛み、等。
　万能鎮痛効果ならびに抗炎症作用があり、副作用が少ない。
lines.english: An over-the-counter analgesic whose primary active ingredient is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug. Indicated for headaches, toothaches, menstrual pain, muscle pain, joint pain, lower-back pain, pain from bruises or fractures, pain from injuries, and more. It provides broad-spectrum pain relief and anti-inflammatory action with few side effects.

lines.japanese:
通常、非ステロイド性消炎鎮痛剤（イブプロフェン等）には、副作用として酵
素の阻害による胃粘膜障害があり、胃壁に対する負担が大きい。
lines.english: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen ordinarily risk damaging the gastric mucosa, as their inhibition of enzymes places a considerable burden on the stomach lining.

lines.japanese:
酵素には全身の細胞に存在する構成型酵素と、炎症部にのみ出現する誘導型酵
素がある。
　このうち善玉とも言える構成型酵素を阻害した場合、消化器症状が顕著なもの
となりやすい。
　そこで抗炎症作用を誘引するため核膜内の誘導型酵素のみを選択的に阻害する
薬が主流となった。
lines.english: Cells throughout the body contain constitutive enzymes, while inducible enzymes appear only at sites of inflammation. Inhibiting the constitutive enzymes—the “good” enzymes of the two—tends to produce pronounced gastrointestinal symptoms. Drugs that selectively inhibit the inducible enzymes within the nuclear membrane therefore became the standard means of producing an anti-inflammatory effect.

lines.japanese:
ズツートレチャウーノは、さらに副作用の少ない鎮痛剤を目指して大野木製薬
によって開発された。
　両酵素に加え、リポキシゲナーゼをも阻害することで、腫れをもたらすロイコ
トリエンの合成を抑制。副作用なく従来品以上の的確な著効をもたらした。
　市販薬としてはもっとも広く愛用されている。
lines.english: Headache-Be-Gone was developed by Oonoki Pharmaceuticals in pursuit of an analgesic with even fewer side effects. In addition to those two enzymes, it inhibits lipoxygenase, suppressing the synthesis of the leukotrienes that cause swelling. This produced more targeted and potent effects than earlier products, without adverse reactions. It is the most widely used over-the-counter medication of its kind.

lines.japanese:
なお、ズツートレチャウーノも旧製品では誘導型酵素選択的阻害剤であった。
　後、研究によってバージョンアップが計られ、リポキシゲナーゼ阻害版のズツ
ートレチャウーノが誕生したのである。
lines.english: The original formulation of Headache-Be-Gone was likewise a selective inhibitor of inducible enzymes. Later research produced an upgraded formulation: a version of Headache-Be-Gone designed to inhibit lipoxygenase.

lines.japanese:
主成分に「優しさ」と明記されていることでも有名。
　ぶっちゃけ、成分表示の虚偽にあたる。
lines.english: It is also famous for listing “kindness” as its main ingredient. Frankly, that's false labeling.

lines.japanese:
雑誌を閉じてため息をついた時、樋口章二が何を
言うか、忍にはだいたい予想がついていた。
lines.english: When Shouji Higuchi closed the magazine with a sigh, Shinobu already had a fair idea what he was going to say.

lines.japanese: 「……男はバイクだぜ」
lines.english: “...A man's gotta have a motorcycle.”

lines.japanese: 「男は、バイク」
lines.english: “A man... and a motorcycle.”

lines.japanese:
言葉を反復してみる。
　いまいち実感が湧かない。
lines.english: He repeated the words to himself. They didn't quite ring true.

lines.japanese: 「なぜ、バイク？」
lines.english: “Why a motorcycle?”

lines.japanese: 「そいつを語るには、言葉は不便すぎるぜ……」
lines.english: “Words are too clumsy to explain a thing like that...”

lines.japanese:
わけがわからない。
　ただ直感で、こう思った。
lines.english: It made no sense. But instinct told him one thing.

lines.japanese: （硬派病が出た）
lines.english: (His macho fever is back.)

hyperlinks.preview: A condition in which one imagines an ideal shared by some unspecified collection of men, then mistak

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: A condition in which one imagines an ideal shared by some unspecified collection of men, then mistak

lines.japanese: 「バイクと言っても、原付なんかじゃない」
lines.english: “And when I say motorcycle, I don't mean some moped.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ……やっぱりななはん？」
lines.english: “Then... a seven-fifty, naturally?”

lines.japanese: 「ナナハンか……」
lines.english: “A seven-fifty...”

lines.japanese: 章二はなぜか遠い目をした。
lines.english: For some reason, Shouji gazed into the distance.

lines.japanese: 「悪くない」
lines.english: “Not bad.”

lines.japanese: 「ナナハンだったら、僕も持ってる」
lines.english: “I have a seven-fifty too.”

lines.japanese: 章二は椅子の上でずれた。
lines.english: Shouji slipped sideways in his chair.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだと！？」
lines.english: “Y-you what!?”

lines.japanese: 「古いものだけど」
lines.english: “It's old, though.”

lines.japanese: 「マジか……」
lines.english: “Seriously...?”

lines.japanese: 「けっこう乗ったかな」
lines.english: “I’ve gotten quite a bit of mileage out of it.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ……いつの間に……型はなんだ？」
lines.english: “You... Since when? What model?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと……ＦＴだったかな」
lines.english: “Let's see... I think it was the FT.”

lines.japanese:
「……オレの知識にはないな。
　まさか……ビンテージものだとでも言うのか！？」
lines.english: “...Never heard of it. Don't tell me... it's some vintage machine!?”

lines.japanese: わなわなと震え、
lines.english: He quivered all over.

lines.japanese: 「見せろ！」
lines.english: “Show me!”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。ちょっと待ってて」
lines.english: “Sure. Wait right here.”

lines.japanese: 忍は立ち上がった。
lines.english: Shinobu stood.

lines.japanese: 「章二」
lines.english: “Shouji.”

lines.japanese: 戻ってきた。
lines.english: He was back.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どこだ？」
lines.english: “W-where is it?”

lines.japanese: 少し昂奮している章二。
lines.english: Shouji was visibly excited.

lines.japanese:
いつも無理して作っているクールさが抜けてみっ
ともない感じだ。
lines.english: The cool facade he was always straining to maintain had fallen away. It wasn't a pretty sight.

lines.japanese: 「ナナハンＦＴ」
lines.english: “The Nanahan FT.”

hyperlinks.preview: Made by T○. Sound Nanahan 75○FT. 3-band radio. Manufactured… early 1970s. Capable of FM transmission

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Made by T○. Sound Nanahan 75○FT. 3-band radio. Manufactured… early 1970s. Capable of FM transmission

lines.japanese: 「バッキャロー！！」
lines.english: “YOU MORON!!”

lines.japanese:
「ＧＴもあったけど、
　そっちは捨ててしまったみたいだ」
lines.english: “There was a GT too, but I think that one got thrown away.”

lines.japanese: 「もういい……」
lines.english: “I'm done...”

lines.japanese:
「……なにが乗ってるだ……紛らわしい言い方しや
　がって……この腹黒野郎が」
lines.english: “…‘Quite a bit of mileage,’ my ass… Talk about misleading, you devious bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「まだ聴けるかな」
lines.english: “Wonder if I can still pick anything up on it.”

lines.japanese: いろいろといじってると、音が鳴り出した。
lines.english: He fiddled with it until sound crackled out.

lines.japanese: 「すごい」
lines.english: “Amazing.”

lines.japanese: 章二がそれを手に取る。
lines.english: Shouji took it from him.

lines.japanese:
「アナログラジオじゃねぇか。
　よくこんなもん取ってあったな」
lines.english: “An analog radio? I can't believe you held on to this thing.”

lines.japanese: 「別の意味でびびったぜ」
lines.english: “Now I'm shocked for a whole different reason.”

lines.japanese:
「とにかく、オレ様が欲しいのはラジオなんかじゃ
　ない。バイクだ」
lines.english: “Anyway, what I want isn't some radio. I want a motorcycle.”

lines.japanese: 「免許は？」
lines.english: “Do you have a license?”

lines.japanese: 「……なんとかなる。現物さえありゃいいんだ」
lines.english: “...I'll work something out. All that matters is getting the bike.”

lines.japanese: 「値段はいくらくらいなんだろ」
lines.english: “Wonder how much one costs.”

lines.japanese: 忍は雑誌をぱらぱらとめくった。閉じた。
lines.english: Shinobu flipped through the magazine, then snapped it shut.

lines.japanese: 「……肝臓かな」
lines.english: “...Call it one liver.”

lines.japanese: 「売らん」
lines.english: “Not selling.”

lines.japanese: 「こんなの買えるわけない」
lines.english: “There's no way you can afford one of these.”

lines.japanese: 「バイト頑張れば買える」
lines.english: “I can if I work hard enough.”

lines.japanese: 「そぉかなぁ……」
lines.english: “You really think so...?”

lines.japanese:
「マシーンがいる……男には自分の世界があるんだ
　……そのためにマシーンが……マシーン号が……」
lines.english: “I need a machine… Every man has a world all his own… and for that he needs a machine… the Machine…”

lines.japanese: 悩み出す。
lines.english: He sank into thought.

lines.japanese: （名前はマシーン号か……）
lines.english: (So he’s calling it the Machine…)

lines.japanese: 「ま、見てろ。じきに手に入れてやるさ」
lines.english: “Just watch. I'll have one before long.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいけどね。章二の金だし」
lines.english: “Fine by me. It's your money.”

lines.japanese: 「目標ができるとオレは凄い男だ。見てろよ」
lines.english: “Give me a goal and I'm unstoppable. You'll see.”

lines.japanese:
こうして樋口章二のマシーン獲得の長く険しい旅
がはじまるのである。
lines.english: Thus began Shouji Higuchi’s long and arduous quest to acquire a machine.

lines.japanese: 〈つづく〉
lines.english: 〈TO BE CONTINUED〉

lines.japanese: 「シノ、バイク買ったぞ」
lines.english: “Shino, I bought a motorcycle.”

lines.japanese: 顔を出すなりそう宣言した。
lines.english: He announced it the moment he appeared.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだって？」
lines.english: “...You did what?”

lines.japanese: 「注文したぜ。見てみろ」
lines.english: “Ordered it. Take a look.”

lines.japanese:
ソファの上であずさと対戦型のカードゲームを遊
んでいた忍に、脇に抱えていた封筒を投げる。
lines.english: Shinobu sat on the sofa playing a competitive card game with Azusa. Shouji flung him the envelope tucked under his arm.

lines.japanese: くるくると回転しながら、封筒が忍のもとに飛ぶ。
lines.english: The envelope spun through the air toward Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「あちょー！」
lines.english: “Hii-yah!”

lines.japanese: あずさ（運動神経良）が叩き落とした。
lines.english: Azusa (good reflexes) swatted it down.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんてことしやがる！」
lines.english: “Wh-what the hell was that for!?”

lines.japanese: 無様に這いずり、封筒の砂を払う章二だ。
lines.english: Shouji scrambled after it on all fours and brushed the sand off the envelope.

lines.japanese: 「今いいとこなんだから邪魔すんでね」
lines.english: “We're at the good part, so don't bug us.”

lines.japanese: じろりとソファ上の戦場を眺める。
lines.english: He glared at the battlefield spread across the sofa.

lines.japanese: 「まーたやってんのか」
lines.english: “Playing that again?”

lines.japanese: 「うるさい！」
lines.english: “Shut up!”

lines.japanese: 自分の椅子を引き寄せ、背もたれを前に座る。
lines.english: He dragged over his chair and sat astride it, facing the backrest.

lines.japanese: 「おまえの負けっぷりを見届けてやる」
lines.english: “I'll stick around and watch you lose.”

lines.japanese: 「……負けぬ」
lines.english: “...I will not lose.”

lines.japanese: 「いざ」
lines.english: “Come!”

lines.japanese: ゲームはまだはじまったばかりだった。
lines.english: The game had only just begun.

lines.japanese:
無数のカードから選んだ６０枚（カード一種類に
つき四枚まで）を一つのデッキをそれぞれ持ち寄り、
対戦するのである。
lines.english: Each player assembled a sixty-card deck from countless possibilities (with no more than four copies of any one card) and brought it to battle.

lines.japanese:
最初の手札は７枚で、交互に一枚ずつ引いて戦う。
　いろいろなカードを駆使して、相手のライフを０
にしたら勝ち。
lines.english: They began with seven cards in hand, then took turns drawing one at a time. Using every card at their disposal, they tried to reduce the opponent's life total to zero. Whoever did so won.

lines.japanese: 「デュエルはパワーだね」
lines.english: “A duel is all about power.”

lines.japanese:
あずさは自分の初期の手札を見て、うんうんと頷
いた。
lines.english: Azusa studied her opening hand and nodded sagely to herself.

lines.japanese:
敵のモンスターは火力で除去しながら、パワフル
なクリーチャーで一方的に攻撃するデッキだ。
lines.english: Her deck burned enemy monsters off the field, leaving her powerful creatures free to attack.

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Go ahead.”

lines.japanese: 先行は忍だ。
lines.english: Shinobu had the first turn.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、行くね」
lines.english: “All right, here goes.”

lines.japanese: 「負けたじゃねぇか」
lines.english: “You lost.”

lines.japanese: 「うっうっう……」
lines.english: “Snf... snf...”

lines.japanese: 素知らぬ顔で、忍はデッキをシャッフルしている。
lines.english: Shinobu shuffled his deck with a look of perfect innocence.

lines.japanese:
「だってね、だってね、なんか最初のターンに０マ
　ナで出てくるクリーチャーがいて、それ生贄に捧
　げて４マナとか使えるカードがあってね」
lines.english: “But, but, listen! On the first turn he played some creature for zero mana, then sacrificed it and played this card that gives him four mana or something!”

lines.japanese:
「なんかいろいろぐるぐるまわってこっちに順番
　まわってくる前にライフなくなっちゃったよ？」
lines.english: “Then all this stuff kept going around and around, and I was out of life before I even got a turn!”

lines.japanese: 「１ターンキルという小さな奇跡が起こったんだ」
lines.english: “A small miracle known as a one-turn kill occurred.”

lines.japanese: 「……おまえもそんなえげつないの使ってやるな」
lines.english: “...You didn't have to use something that nasty on her.”

lines.japanese: 「手加減無礼なり」
lines.english: “Holding back would be an insult.”

lines.japanese: 「確かに……」
lines.english: “True...”

lines.japanese: 「もう一個の、ゾンビデッキの方でやる？」
lines.english: “Want to try my other deck? The zombie one?”

lines.japanese: 「ゾンビきらーい！」
lines.english: “I hate zombies!”

lines.japanese: あずさはゾンビが嫌いだった。
lines.english: Azusa hated zombies.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ休憩っと」
lines.english: “Okay, break time.”

lines.japanese: 忍は大きく伸びをした。
lines.english: Shinobu gave a tremendous stretch.

lines.japanese: 「それで、バイク買ったって？」
lines.english: “So, you said you bought a motorcycle?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、これだ」
lines.english: “Yeah. This one.”

lines.japanese: 渡されたパンフレットを見る。
lines.english: He studied the brochure Shouji handed him.

lines.japanese: 「……大型じゃないんだ」
lines.english: “...It's not a big bike.”

lines.japanese: 「国のせいだ」
lines.english: “Blame the government.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ないので、５０ＣＣからはじめることにした」
lines.english: “I had no choice, so I'm starting at fifty cc.”

lines.japanese: 「だがこいつは原付だがけっこう高いぞ」
lines.english: “It may be a moped, but it's an expensive one.”

lines.japanese: 「……ローマの休日に出てきたやつに似てるね」
lines.english: “...It looks like the one from Roman Holiday.”

lines.japanese: 「それだ」
lines.english: “That's the one.”

lines.japanese: 「全然ハードじゃないじゃん」
lines.english: “That's not macho at all.”

lines.japanese:
「フォルムの美しさが硬派なんだよ。
　猿はモンキーにでも乗ってろって感じだな」
lines.english: “The beauty of its lines is what makes it macho. Monkeys can stick to riding Monkeys.”

lines.japanese: 「……まんまじゃん……」
lines.english: “...That's literally what they're called...”

lines.japanese: 「いつ来るの？」
lines.english: “When does it arrive?”

lines.japanese: 「今月末に納車だ」
lines.english: “Delivery's set for the end of the month.”

lines.japanese: 「ここに持ってきてよ」
lines.english: “Have them bring it here.”
“What...”

lines.japanese: 章二は虚を突かれた。
lines.english: Azusa had caught him off guard.

lines.japanese: 「バイク乗ってみたい」
lines.english: “I wanna ride a motorcycle.”

lines.japanese: 助けを求めて忍を見る。
lines.english: He looked to Shinobu for help.

lines.japanese: 「乗ってみたい」
lines.english: “I want to ride it too.”
Two against one.

lines.japanese:
「……こいつはフットペダルだから、
　ちょっと難しいんだぞ？」
lines.english: “...It's got a foot pedal, so it's harder than it looks, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「バイクこうやって乗ってるの、やってみたい」
lines.english: “I wanna do that thing where you ride like this.”

lines.japanese: 「いいね、楽しそう」
lines.english: “That looks fun.”

lines.japanese:
あずさが椅子をバイクに見立てて、ハングを切っ
ている。
lines.english: Azusa straddled the chair as though it were a motorcycle and hung off the seat into a turn.

lines.japanese: 膝が地面をこするほど傾き、すてんと転んでしまう。
lines.english: She leaned until her knee nearly scraped the floor, then toppled over.
“Whoa.”

lines.japanese:
たいしたもので、危なげもなく手をついた。
　椅子は音を立てて転がった。
lines.english: Impressively, she caught herself without the slightest trouble. The chair went clattering away.

lines.japanese: 「おまえには乗せない」
lines.english: “You're not getting on it.”

lines.japanese:
「えー」
「えー」
lines.english: “Aww.” “Aww.”

lines.japanese: 「大事に乗るんだ！」
lines.english: “I'm going to take good care of it!”

lines.japanese: 「硬派じゃなーい」
lines.english: “Not very macho.”

lines.japanese: 「なんか違う。今の章二かっこわるい」
lines.english: “Something's off. You looked really lame just now, Shouji.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なにぃ……」
lines.english: “Wh-what...?”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあちゃんと乗るから、とりあえずここに納車
　しようよ」
lines.english: “Then I'll be really careful. Just have them deliver it here.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはおまえ……」
lines.english: “No, now hold on...”

lines.japanese: 「一人がみんなのために」
lines.english: “One for all.”

lines.japanese: 「いつ来たんだおまえは！！」
lines.english: “WHEN DID YOU GET HERE!?”

lines.japanese: 〈つづく〉
lines.english: 〈TO BE CONTINUED〉

lines.japanese: 納車当日。
lines.english: Delivery day.

lines.japanese:
指定先を工場にして、章二は待っていた。
　少年のような忍耐力で、入口に立っていた。
lines.english: Shouji had given the factory as the delivery address and was waiting there. He stood at the entrance with all the patience of a little boy.

lines.japanese: 「章二、中で待ってたら？」
lines.english: “Why don't you wait inside, Shouji?”

lines.japanese: 「ここはわかりにくいから、立ってないとな」
lines.english: “This place is hard to find. Somebody has to stand out here.”
“Right...”

lines.japanese: 五分後。
lines.english: Five minutes later.

lines.japanese: 「章二」
lines.english: “Shouji.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ？　用事ならあとで―――」
lines.english: “What? If you need something, it can wait—”

lines.japanese: 「僕もつきあおうと思って」
lines.english: “Thought I'd keep you company.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうか」
lines.english: “...Yeah.”

lines.japanese: カップを差し出す。
lines.english: He held out a cup.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、好きなやつ」
lines.english: “Here. Your favorite.”

lines.japanese: 中身はコーラだ。
lines.english: It was filled with cola.

lines.japanese: 「悪い」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: あとは静かでおだやかな時間が流れるのみであった。
lines.english: After that, time passed quietly and peacefully.

lines.japanese: 「電話、してみたらどうかな？」
lines.english: “Maybe you should call them?”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだな」
lines.english: “...Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
あまりにも遅れているため、忍がそう提案したの
だった。
lines.english: The delivery was so late that Shinobu finally made the suggestion.

lines.japanese:
章二は携帯を取り出す。
　アンテナを見ると、五本とも立っている。
lines.english: Shouji took out his phone. All five signal bars were showing.

lines.japanese: 「よし」
lines.english: “Good.”

lines.japanese: 店に電話をかけた。
lines.english: He called the store.

lines.japanese: 「どうだった？」
lines.english: “What did they say?”

lines.japanese: 「配達には時間通りに出たらしい」
lines.english: “Apparently it went out for delivery on time.”

lines.japanese: 「迷ってるのかな」
lines.english: “Maybe the driver got lost.”

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、使えない店だぜ。醒めるな」
lines.english: “Tch. What a useless shop. Way to kill the mood.”

lines.japanese: 「中で待とうか」
lines.english: “Want to wait inside?”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだな」
lines.english: “...Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
二人は諦めて、工場に入った。
　結局この日、原付が納車されることはなかった。
lines.english: The two of them gave up and went into the factory. In the end, the moped never arrived that day.

lines.japanese:
原付を乗せたトラックごと、どこかに失踪してし
まったのだそうだ。
lines.english: Apparently the entire delivery truck, moped and all, vanished somewhere.

lines.japanese: 返金はされなかったという―――
lines.english: Apparently, no refund was issued—

lines.japanese: 〈つづく〉
lines.english: 〈TO BE CONTINUED〉

lines.japanese: 「あ、章二だ」
lines.english: “Oh, there's Shouji.”

lines.japanese: 「……おまえらか」
lines.english: “...It's you two.”

lines.japanese:
「最近、朝も夕方も顔を出さない裏切り者の章二だ
　わ」
lines.english: “Look who it is—Shouji the traitor, who never shows his face in the morning or the evening anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「言うなメガネ……不可抗力だ」
lines.english: “Don't call me that, Four-eyes... It was beyond my control.”

lines.japanese:
「これ外してどんなことになっても知らないわよ？
　あんた責任とれんの、ああ？」
lines.english: “If I take these off, whatever happens is on you. Got that? You ready to take responsibility, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「極道の妻か、おまえは」
lines.english: “What are you, a yakuza wife?”

lines.japanese: 「だいたい、何が起こるんだ」
lines.english: “What would happen, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「顔の一部なのよ……」
lines.english: “They're part of my face...”

lines.japanese: 「わからん」
lines.english: “I don't get it.”

lines.japanese:
「とりあえず久しぶりだけど……
　なんかボロボロなのはどうして？」
lines.english: “Anyway, it's been a while... Why do you look like hell?”

lines.japanese: 壁に背をつけて、その場でへたり込む章二だった。
lines.english: Shouji leaned against the wall, slid down it, and crumpled to the floor.

lines.japanese: 「こらこら」
lines.english: “Hey, now.”

lines.japanese: 「……もう限界だ」
lines.english: “...I've reached my limit.”

lines.japanese: 衣服は汚れ、髪は乱れ、肌も張りを失っている。
lines.english: His clothes were filthy, his hair disheveled, and his skin drawn.

lines.japanese: 「あんた、ちょっと臭うわよ？　お風呂入ってる？」
lines.english: “You kind of stink. Have you been taking baths?”

lines.japanese: 「入ってない」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「何してんの」
lines.english: “What have you been doing?”

lines.japanese: 「話せば長いことなんだが……」
lines.english: “It's a long story...”

lines.japanese: 横倒しに倒れた。
lines.english: He toppled sideways.
“...So... hungry...”

lines.japanese: 「な、なに、なにー！？」
lines.english: “Wh-what? What is it!?”

lines.japanese:
息も絶え絶えに何か呟く。
　仲間の顔を見て、張りつめていた糸が切れたのか
も知れない。
lines.english: He mumbled something, barely breathing. Perhaps the sight of his friends had finally snapped the thread that had kept him going.

lines.japanese: 忍が耳を近づける。
lines.english: Shinobu bent down to listen.

lines.japanese:
「え、なに？　三日もほとんど何も口にしてない？
　捜査であと一歩のところまで追いつめて、食料調
　達せずに山奥に追跡？」
lines.english: “What? You've barely eaten anything in three days? You almost had your target cornered, then chased them into the mountains without stopping for food?”

lines.japanese:
「トラックの荷台に乗り込んで山奥まで？
　徒歩で帰ってきた？」
lines.english: “You climbed into the back of a truck and rode it into the mountains? Then walked all the way back?”

lines.japanese: 「……何者よアンタは」
lines.english: “...Who even are you?”

lines.japanese: 「あとは……任せた……」
lines.english: “The rest... is up to you...”

lines.japanese: 「任せるな任せるな」
lines.english: “Don't dump it on us! Don't!”

lines.japanese: 目を閉じる。
lines.english: He closed his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「……気絶した」
lines.english: “...He passed out.”

lines.japanese: 「彼、なんだって？」
lines.english: “What did he say?”

lines.japanese: 「わからない……」
lines.english: “I don't know...”

lines.japanese: 「とりあえずなんか食べさせないと。ごめん、笛子」
lines.english: “We need to feed him. Sorry, Fueko.”

lines.japanese:
笛子は少しだけ眉をひそめた。
　すぐに元に戻る。若干の穏やかなものになって。
lines.english: Fueko frowned for just a moment. When her face settled again, it had softened a little.

lines.japanese: 「……もう。楽しみにしてたのに」
lines.english: “...Honestly. I was looking forward to it.”

lines.japanese: 「今度つきあうから、参考書選び」
lines.english: “I'll help you pick out study guides another time.”

lines.japanese: 「いーわよ。別にすぐいるってもんでもないし」
lines.english: “Fine. It's not like I need them right away.”

lines.japanese: 「それよりそこの難民をなんとかしないとね」
lines.english: “Anyway, we'd better do something about our refugee over there.”

lines.japanese: 「……生き返ったぜ」
lines.english: “...Back from the dead.”

lines.japanese:
「ごちそーさま。
　便乗していいもの食べさせてもらいました」
lines.english: “Thanks for the meal. I got to tag along and have something wonderful too.”

lines.japanese: 「おそまつさんです」
lines.english: “It was nothing.”

lines.japanese:
卓上に並べられた大量の皿。
　三人でたいらげた、忍の手料理だ。
lines.english: A mountain of empty plates covered the table. The three of them had polished off Shinobu's cooking.

lines.japanese: 「みんなで食べるとんまい」
lines.english: “Everything tastes better when we eat together.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、洗うわね」
lines.english: “Oh, I'll do the dishes.”

lines.japanese: 「いいのに」
lines.english: “You don't have to.”

lines.japanese: 「体で返すわ」
lines.english: “I'll repay you with my body.”

lines.japanese: 笛子、気づかない。
lines.english: Fueko did not notice.

lines.japanese: 「さーて、やるか」
lines.english: “All right, let's do this.”

lines.japanese: 腕まくり。
lines.english: She rolled up her sleeves.

lines.japanese: 「せいぜいしっかり働くんだな」
lines.english: “Make sure you earn your keep.”

lines.japanese: 「あんたも働けい！」
lines.english: “You get to work too!”

lines.japanese: 「紅茶淹れたよ」
lines.english: “I made tea.”

lines.japanese:
「うわ、いい香り。ふれーばーふれーばー。
　どこの紅茶？」
lines.english: “Oh, that smells wonderful. Flavor, flavor. What kind of tea is it?”

lines.japanese: 「姉しか知らず」
lines.english: “Only my sister knows.”

lines.japanese: 「袋見せ―――ベッ、ヴェノアっ！？」
lines.english: “Let me see the package—B-Benoist!?”

lines.japanese: 包みを見て、笛子はのけぞった。
lines.english: Fueko recoiled when she saw the package.

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あんたの姉上様、あなどれないわね……」
lines.english: “Your illustrious sister is not to be underestimated...”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
「ここの紅茶、日本にしか輸出してないのよ。
　日本でもなんとかってデパートでしか買えない
　ってことだから」
lines.english: “They only export this tea to Japan. And even here, you can only get it at some department store or other.”

lines.japanese:
「いやー、あの若さで一軒家持つだけのことはある
　ってことね……勉強しよ、私も」
lines.english: “No wonder she owns her own house at her age. I'd better study harder myself.”

lines.japanese: 「同じ店のものと思われるスコーンもあるよ」
lines.english: “Looks like there are scones from the same shop too.”

lines.japanese: 「悪くない」
lines.english: “Not bad.”

lines.japanese: 「異様にんまいな、これ」
lines.english: “These are freakishly good.”

lines.japanese: 手掴みでわしゃわしゃ食べる二人だ。
lines.english: The two of them shoveled the scones down with their bare hands.

lines.japanese: 「わ、私にも！」
lines.english: “S-save some for me!”

lines.japanese:
争奪戦。
　別腹とはよく言ったもので―――
lines.english: A feeding frenzy. They weren't kidding about having a separate stomach for dessert—

lines.japanese:
スコーンをたいらげて、三人は同時に吐息を落と
した。
lines.english: When they'd demolished the scones, all three of them sighed at once.

lines.japanese: 「食った」
lines.english: “I'm stuffed.”

lines.japanese: 「……幸せだわ」
lines.english: “...This is bliss.”

lines.japanese: それぞれソファに身を預けて、昼寝の勢いだ。
lines.english: They sprawled across the sofa, ready to nap the afternoon away.

lines.japanese: 「こんな幸せな土曜日、滅多にないわ……」
lines.english: “Saturdays this perfect don't come often...”

lines.japanese:
「これでこの汗くさい男がいなければどんなにいい
　か」
lines.english: “If only this sweaty man weren't here, it would be even better.”

lines.japanese: 「……なめるなよ、この汗を……」
lines.english: “...Don't mock this sweat...”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ」
lines.english: “Oh, right.”

lines.japanese: 一人、身を起こす。
lines.english: Shinobu alone sat up.

lines.japanese: 「なんでレスホームになってたわけ？」
lines.english: “How did you end up less-home, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「レスホームってアンタ……」
lines.english: “‘Less-home’? Honestly...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そのことだが……」
lines.english: “Right. About that...”

lines.japanese: 「原付を追っていた」
lines.english: “I was chasing my moped.”

lines.japanese: 「……って、このあいだ盗難されたアレ？」
lines.english: “...The one that was stolen the other day?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ！」
lines.english: “Exactly!”

lines.japanese: 「お金返してもらえなかったっていう？」
lines.english: “The one they wouldn't refund?”

lines.japanese: 「いかにも！」
lines.english: “The very same!”

lines.japanese: 「その原付を追っていた、つまり？」
lines.english: “You were chasing it. As in...?”

lines.japanese: 「見つけたんだ」
lines.english: “I found it.”

lines.japanese: そして章二は語り始めた。
lines.english: And Shouji began his tale.

lines.japanese:
「盗難届けは出したがこんなご時世だ。
　そうそう見つかるものでもないと思ってた」
lines.english: “I reported it stolen, but these are the times we live in. I wasn't expecting it to turn up anytime soon.”

lines.japanese: 「そこでオレは、自力で捜査を開始することにした」
lines.english: “So I decided to launch my own investigation.”

lines.japanese:
「といっても本職の警察じゃないからな。
　毎日歩き回ったわけじゃない」
lines.english: “I'm no real cop or anything. It's not like I spent every day walking the streets.”

lines.japanese: 「ところがある日、偶然オレは見たんだ」
lines.english: “Then one day, by pure chance, I saw it.”

lines.japanese:
「……オレ自らがデザインした代紋が塗装された、
　原付をな―――」
lines.english: “...A moped bearing the crest I designed myself—”

lines.japanese: 「アホか」
lines.english: “Idiot.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえにノーズアートの何がわかる！」
lines.english: “What do you know about nose art!?”

lines.english: “I think so...”

lines.japanese: 「どうして」
「―――たすけた？」
lines.english: “—did you save me?”

lines.japanese: 回答不能。
lines.english: Answer: impossible.

lines.japanese: 「貴宮君はあたしを助けた―――あってる？」
lines.english: “You saved me—is that right, Atemiya?”

lines.japanese: 回答可能。
lines.english: Answer: possible.

lines.japanese:
言語化してしまうと、少女あずさとの距離が変化
してしまういそうな気がした。
lines.english: He felt that putting it into words might alter the distance between himself and the girl, Azusa.

lines.japanese:
これ以上の接近は無意味。
　思考はそう告げていた。
lines.english: Further approach served no purpose. That was the conclusion his mind returned.

lines.japanese:
そもそも助けたこと自体が誤りだったと今は思う。
　放置すべきだった。
lines.english: Now he thought that rescuing her at all had been a mistake. He should have left her alone.

lines.japanese:
忍がコースを変えれば良かった。
　失敗だ。
lines.english: Shinobu should have taken a different route. Failure.

lines.japanese:
だいぶ印象づけられたのだろうなと思う。
　あずさは忍が施設通いをしていることを忘れない
だろう。
lines.english: He thought he must have made quite an impression on her. Azusa would not forget that Shinobu went to the facility.

lines.japanese:
ならばある程度、監視下に置いておくという手も
ある。
lines.english: One option, then, was to keep her under a limited degree of observation.

lines.japanese:
そう……もう忍とあずさは無関係ではないのだ。
　下手な対応はできない。
lines.english: Yes... A connection now existed between Shinobu and Azusa. He could not afford to handle this poorly.

lines.japanese: 慎重に、口を開いた。
lines.english: He chose his words carefully.

lines.japanese: 「……あってる、と思う」
lines.english: “...I think that's right.”

lines.japanese:
あずさの態度が目に見えて軟化している。
　流れは止まらないだろう。
lines.english: Azusa’s manner was softening before his eyes. This would probably keep going.

lines.japanese:
あずさは忍に感染・発症している。
　侵略してしまったのだ。
lines.english: Azusa had become infected with Shinobu. The symptoms had manifested. He had invaded her.

lines.japanese: もう退けない。
lines.english: Too late to retreat.

lines.japanese: 「そう、なんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「貴宮くんは、どうしてあたしを―――」
lines.english: “Atemiya, why did you—”

lines.japanese:
（１／問題になると思った）（２／命令された）
（３／助けない方が不自然だと思った）
（４／助けたかった）
lines.english:
(1 / I thought it might cause a problem.)
(2 / I was ordered to.)
(3 / I thought not helping would look unnatural.)
(4 / I wanted to help.)

lines.japanese: いくつかの候補を検討し、絞り込んだ。
lines.english: He considered several possibilities and narrowed them down.

lines.japanese: 「友達が、欲しいんだ」
lines.english: “I want a friend.”

lines.japanese:
告げる忍の表情に、感情的な変化はない。
　が、友人のいないあずさは、そんな機微さえ読み
取れない。
lines.english: Shinobu's expression showed no emotional change as he said it. But Azusa, who had no friends herself, could not read even that nuance.

lines.japanese: 「どうすればいい？」
lines.english: “What do I do?”

lines.japanese: 「どうすればって……そんなの……」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what do you do...? Well...”

lines.japanese: 「僕、慣れていないんだ。人付き合い」
lines.english: “I'm not used to being around people.”

lines.japanese: 感情の欠落に、あずさは気付かない。
lines.english: Azusa did not notice the absence of emotion.

lines.japanese: 「だから、よくわからないんだ」
lines.english: “So I don't really know.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしにもわかんないよ、いないし……」
lines.english: “I don't know either. I don't have any friends...”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん」
lines.english: “Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 立ち去ろうとする。
lines.english: He turned to leave.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ちょっと！　ちょっと待ってってばっ！？」
lines.english: “H-hey! Wait a second—I said wait!?”

lines.japanese: 腕を捕まれた。
lines.english: She caught hold of his arm.

lines.japanese: 捕まれた部分を、忍はじっと見た。
lines.english: Shinobu stared at the place where she'd grabbed him.

lines.japanese: 「知ってる、知ってるよ！」
lines.english: “I know! I know what to do!”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「友達、の作り方、知ってる……思いついた」
lines.english: “I know how to make friends... I just thought of it.”

lines.japanese: ためらいがちに。
lines.english: She spoke hesitantly.

lines.japanese: 「教えて、くれる？」
lines.english: “Will you tell me?”

lines.japanese:
あずさは頷く。
　顔色を傾けて隠したまま、
lines.english: Azusa nodded. Her face still turned aside and hidden,

lines.japanese: 「あたしたちが、友達になれば、いいと思うよ」
lines.english: “I think we should be friends.”

lines.japanese: 却下の対象たりえた。
lines.english: It was a proposal he could reject.

lines.japanese:
忍に必要なのは、対象との接触手段である。
　対象とあずさは無関係。
　あずさに頼る意味はない。
lines.english: What Shinobu needed was a means of contacting his targets. The targets and Azusa were unconnected. There was no reason to rely on her.

lines.japanese: 断りの言葉を形作ろうとして、しかし思考を重ねる。
lines.english: He began to frame a refusal, then thought further.

lines.japanese: 「だめ……かな？」
lines.english: “Would that... be bad?”

lines.japanese: 「いや」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね……それはいい手だと思うよ」
lines.english: “You're right... I think that's a good plan.”

lines.japanese:
忍は狙撃型の監視策を放棄。
　以降、対象に接近し交友をもって見張る方針へ、
転換するに至るのである。
lines.english: Shinobu abandoned the sniper-style approach to surveillance. From then on, he would close in on his targets and monitor them by befriending them.

lines.japanese: あずさをその先兵として―――
lines.english: With Azusa as the vanguard—

lines.japanese: 嘘である。
lines.english: That is a lie.

lines.japanese:
ちなみに丸目蔵人佐長恵（まるめ・くらんどのすけ・ながよし）は、肥後（現
代の熊本）出身の剣豪で、実在の人物である。
lines.english: Incidentally, Marume Kurandonosuke Nagayoshi was a master swordsman from Higo (present-day Kumamoto) and a real historical figure.

lines.japanese:
天文９年（１５４０）生まれ。
　幼い頃から剣の道に生き、京に出ては新陰流始祖と言われる上泉伊勢守信綱
（かみいずみ・いせのかみ・のぶつな）のもとで修行をした。
　後にはタイ捨流の開祖ともなった、屈指の剣豪である。
lines.english: Born in Tenbun 9 (1540). He devoted his life to swordsmanship from childhood, later traveling to Kyoto to study under Kamiizumi Ise-no-kami Nobutsuna, the reputed founder of Shinkage-ryu. He later founded Taisha-ryu and was one of the foremost masters of the sword.

lines.japanese:
しかし帰郷し九州にて島津との戦に出た蔵人佐は、敵の罠にかかり多くの部下
を死傷させてしまう。
　それは剣の腕ではなく、戦としての判断力における敗北と言えた。
　以降、蔵人佐は零落。９０歳でその生涯を閉じることになる。
lines.english: After returning home, however, Kurandonosuke went to war against the Shimazu in Kyushu and fell into an enemy trap, with many of his men killed or wounded. It was a defeat not of swordsmanship but of judgment on the battlefield. Kurandonosuke fell into decline thereafter. He died at the age of ninety.

lines.japanese: もちろんのことながら、恋とか言わない。
lines.english: Naturally, he never said anything like “love.”

lines.japanese:
お茶の一種……ではなく、地元のこと。
　地元民のことを指す場合もある。
lines.english: Not a kind of tea… It means the local area. It can also refer to the locals.

lines.japanese:
非難の意味を持つ指弾とは関係なく、武術における指を用いた投擲の技。
　如意珠とも呼ばれることもある。
　ちなみに本来の意味における如意珠は、意のままに願いをかなえる宝珠という
もので、意匠の施された小さな宝珠のことを指し、お守りや装飾として用いられ
る。
lines.english: Despite sharing its name with the Japanese word for “condemnation,” this is a martial-arts technique for launching objects with the fingers. It is also sometimes called the “wish-fulfilling jewel.” In its original sense, that name refers to a precious orb said to grant any wish: a small, decoratively worked jewel used as an amulet or ornament.

lines.japanese:
葉子の用いる指弾は、漢字を開いていることから安全性に対する配慮がされて
いるよう錯覚させるが、そのような事実はまったくない。
　お子様の手が届かない場所に保管するべきである。
lines.english: Writing the name of Youko’s technique in kana rather than kanji may suggest that some thought has been given to safety, but nothing could be further from the truth. Keep out of reach of children.

lines.japanese:
威力の方は、たいしたものはない。
　この技によって相手に致命傷を与えることは困難である。
　また命中精度も１０メートルを離れるとほとんど当たらなくなり、近距離にお
いて牽制に用いるのに適した技であると言える。
　使用できるのであれば拳銃の方が良い。
lines.english: Its power is nothing extraordinary. It would be difficult to inflict a fatal wound with this technique. Its accuracy also drops to nearly zero beyond ten meters, making it best suited to keeping an opponent at bay at close range. If you can use one, a handgun is better.

lines.japanese:
紅緒あずさがいつも草原にいることを忍が知った
のは、週に一度の通院を三度繰り返した頃だった。
lines.english: Shinobu realized that Azusa Benio was always in the meadow around his third weekly trip to the doctor.

lines.japanese:
引っ越し三週間目。
　学校での生活も同じだけ。
lines.english: Three weeks since the move. Three weeks of school, too.

lines.japanese: 慣れ……すなわち日常化。
lines.english: Familiarity... in other words, becoming routine.

lines.japanese:
寡黙で優等生でも劣等生でもない少年が、学期途
中から教室の片隅に加わるという比較的物珍しい
イベントも、すでに鮮度を失って久しい。
lines.english: A quiet boy, neither an honor student nor at the bottom of the class, had appeared in one corner of the classroom midway through the term. Even that relatively unusual event had long since ceased to be a novelty.

lines.japanese: 相変わらず、友人はできない。
lines.english: He still had no friends.
(...Sigh.)

lines.japanese:
そのことについては内心いろいろと思うところ
のある忍で、ことあるごとに吐息を呑み込む羽目
になっている。
lines.english: Shinobu had all sorts of private thoughts on the subject, and found himself swallowing a sigh at every turn.

lines.japanese: 幼い集団には不思議なローカルルールがあるものだ。
lines.english: Groups of children had strange local rules of their own.

lines.japanese:
三週間友人ができなかったら、だいたいそのまま
である。
lines.english: If you had made no friends after three weeks, things generally stayed that way.

lines.japanese:
人間はグループ化する。
　これは男女とも変わりない。
lines.english: People formed groups. Boys and girls were no different.

lines.japanese:
居場所は早期に見つけねばならず、機会を失えば
孤立してしまう可能性は高い。
lines.english: You had to find your place early. Miss the opportunity and you were likely to end up alone.

lines.japanese:
今の忍がそうだった。
　孤立した人間は、いろいろな節目ごとにターゲッ
トにされる危険性を背負う。
lines.english: That was where Shinobu found himself now. And at every turn, anyone isolated ran the risk of becoming a target.

lines.japanese: そういうものだ。
lines.english: That was how these things worked.

lines.japanese:
唯一残された選択肢は、可能な限り大人しくして
いること、だ。
lines.english: The only option left to him was to keep as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

lines.japanese:
幸い忍は、生来目立つタイプではない。
　会話なく過ぎる時間にも、慣れた。
lines.english: Fortunately, Shinobu was not conspicuous by nature. He was used to hours passing without a word.

lines.japanese: （こんなものか）
lines.english: (I suppose this is how it is.)

lines.japanese:
引っ越してきてからというもの、考える時間だけ
は増えてしまった。
lines.english: Since moving here, if nothing else, he had found himself with far more time to think.

lines.japanese: 歩いている時、余った意識がそうさせるらしかった。
lines.english: When he walked, the idle part of his mind seemed to set him thinking.

lines.japanese: ショートカットの草原で、忍はあずさとすれ違う。
lines.english: In the meadow he used as a shortcut, Shinobu crossed paths with Azusa.

lines.japanese:
通院曜日は一定しない。
　なのにあずさと出会うのは都合四度目だ。
　つまり彼女は毎日ここにいる可能性がある。
lines.english: His appointments did not fall on a fixed day of the week. Yet this made the fourth time he had encountered Azusa. Which meant she might be here every day.

lines.japanese:
草原で二度目に接触した時、あずさのとった不可
解な行動。
lines.english: Azusa's incomprehensible behavior the second time they met in the meadow.

lines.japanese:
あれ以来、両者の間には皮膜が張られている。
　他者と親愛、いずれにも該当しない象徴する何か。
lines.english: Ever since, a membrane had stretched between them. Something symbolic that was neither otherness nor intimacy.

lines.japanese:
半透明、ゼラチン質の膜。
　うすぼけた向こう側に少女の輪郭が霞み、反対に
こちら側の実体をも曖昧にする。
lines.english: A translucent, gelatinous film. Beyond its dim surface the outline of the girl blurred, while his own substance on this side grew equally indistinct.

lines.japanese:
人間関係における溝とは違うものだ。
　今日も所在なく立ち、牽制するような視線を飛ば
してくる。
lines.english: It was not the gulf one usually spoke of between people. Today again, she stood awkwardly, sending him a look of wary defiance.

lines.japanese: （いつも、睨んでくるな）
lines.english: (She always glares at me.)

lines.japanese: （嫌われているんだか知らないけど……）
lines.english: (I don't know if she hates me, but...)

lines.japanese:
（この場所……もしかするとこの子一人の場所だっ
　たのかもしれない）
lines.english: (Maybe this place... used to belong to her alone.)

lines.japanese: してみれば忍は闖入者だ。
lines.english: If so, Shinobu was the intruder.

lines.japanese: （だけどこっちだって、通らないといけない）
lines.english: (But I have to come through here too.)

lines.japanese: 迂回して正規ルートから行くことも出来た。
lines.english: He could have gone around and taken the proper route.

lines.japanese:
なぜか忍はそうしなかった。
　忍が立ち去るまで、決して厳めしい表情を崩さない。
lines.english: For some reason, Shinobu never did. And until he had gone, her forbidding expression never softened.

lines.japanese:
以前のように、何か仕掛けてくることもない。
　忍が歩き。
　あずさが睨み続ける。
lines.english: Nor did she try anything, as she had before. Shinobu walked. Azusa kept glaring.

lines.japanese:
週に一度。
　時には医療上の関係で週に二度や三度ということ
もあったが。
lines.english: Once a week. Sometimes twice or three times, when his medical care required it.

lines.japanese:
あずさはいつも佇んでいたものだ。
　忍が外世界でそうだったように、この奇妙なすれ
違いもまた、二人にとっての日常と化していく。
lines.english: Azusa was always standing there. Just as life in the outside world had become routine for Shinobu, these strange encounters became routine for them both.

lines.japanese: 連綿と。
lines.english: On and on.

lines.japanese: 綿々と。
lines.english: Week after week.

lines.japanese: 積み重なっていった―――
lines.english: Layer upon layer—

lines.japanese:
いつしか、少女の顔から険は薄れていく。
　怒りの風化か、憎悪の霧散か。
lines.english: Before long, the hardness began to fade from the girl's face. Anger weathering away, or hatred dispersing?

lines.japanese: ただ虚実の膜の向こうにあるものを、見守るような。
lines.english: As though she were merely watching whatever lay beyond that membrane of truth and illusion.

lines.japanese:
柔和な他者性が、そこに形成されていった。
　ただの一度も、対話することなく。
lines.english: A gentle otherness took shape there. Without a single word ever passing between them.

lines.japanese:
それは風化でも霧散でもなかった。
　ましてや氷解でもない。
lines.english: It was neither weathering nor dispersal. Still less was it a thaw.

lines.japanese:
相手の個性や歪み、嫌悪の材料などは別次元のこ
ととなっているに過ぎない。
lines.english: The other's personality and distortions—the raw material of dislike— had merely receded into another dimension.

lines.japanese:
ただ過ぎ去り往く相手を……否定するための強い
動機が保てない。
lines.english: There was simply no powerful impulse left to reject... someone who did no more than pass by.

lines.japanese:
優しく触れる方法を、知らなかっただけなのだ。
　噛まれたことしかない子猫は、噛みつく以外の接
触を学ばないはずだ。
lines.english: She simply did not know how to touch gently. A kitten that had only ever been bitten could hardly learn any touch but biting.

lines.japanese:
あずさは見続けた。
　触れず話さずただ、注ぎ続けた。
lines.english: Azusa kept watching. Never touching, never speaking—only pouring her gaze into him.

lines.japanese: 自然な有り様になったのだ―――
lines.english: It became the natural way of things—

lines.japanese: 「……くちんッ」
lines.english: “...Achoo!”

lines.japanese:
一度だけ足を止めて、あずさを見たことがあった。
　少女は鼻をこすって恥ずかしげに顔を伏せた。
　意味はない。
lines.english: Once, Shinobu stopped and looked at Azusa. The girl rubbed her nose and ducked her head in embarrassment. It meant nothing.

lines.japanese:
いつも見る側のあずさだ。
　真正面から見られたことが初めてであったと、た
だそれだけのことだった。
lines.english: Azusa was always the one who watched. It was simply the first time he had looked her full in the face— nothing more.

lines.japanese: そして―――
lines.english: And then—

lines.japanese: その日、紅緒あずさはいなかった。
lines.english: That day, Azusa Benio was not there.

lines.japanese:
胸騒ぎがした。
　いないだけ。
　騒ぐことではない。
lines.english: A sense of foreboding came over him. She simply was not there. That was no cause for alarm.

lines.japanese:
錐のような直感。
　心に持続する苦痛を与える。
　解決しろ。そう命じる。
lines.english: An intuition sharp as the point of an awl. It drove a steady pain into his mind. Resolve this, it commanded.

lines.japanese:
少しは迷っていたのかも知れない。
　やがてつま先を切り返した。三割り増しの速度で。
lines.english: Perhaps he hesitated for a moment. Then he pivoted and retraced his steps—thirty percent faster.

lines.japanese:
言葉がない。
　草に包まれて寝ているのは見たことがある。
lines.english: He had no words. He had seen her asleep amid the grass.

lines.japanese:
しかし土の上に直接、寝息を立てているのは忍の
常識にない行為だ。
lines.english: But lying directly on the dirt, breathing in her sleep, did not fit Shinobu's idea of normal behavior.

lines.japanese:
少女の胸は薄く上下していた。
　シャツに赤土が染みて、夕日の赤でもかき消せな
いほど色づいている。
lines.english: The girl's chest rose and fell shallowly. Red earth stained her shirt, so deeply that even the scarlet sunset could not hide it.

lines.japanese: （でも……良かった）
lines.english: (But... thank goodness.)

lines.japanese:
ほっとしていた。
　複雑な心境だった。
lines.english: He was relieved. His feelings were complicated.

lines.japanese:
今まで暗黙の不可侵状態だった相手を、心配して
しまったのだ。
lines.english: He had worried about someone with whom he shared an unspoken agreement not to interfere with each other.

lines.japanese:
いないものとして扱っていた面が、あったかも知
れない。
lines.english: Perhaps some part of him had treated her as though she did not exist.

lines.japanese:
あずさは刺々しかったし、最近は大人しかったと
はいえ……あんなことがあったのだから。
lines.english: Azusa had always been prickly, and though she had quieted lately... there was what had happened before.

lines.japanese: だけど今、忍は認めざるを得ない。
lines.english: But now, Shinobu had no choice but to admit it.

lines.japanese: （……心配……心配したんだ……きっと）
lines.english: (...Worried... I was worried about her... I think.)

lines.japanese: （この気持ち、ほっとけないって気持ち）
lines.english: (This feeling... that I can't leave her alone.)

lines.japanese: （だってこの子、危なっかしい）
lines.english: (Because this girl always looks like she's about to get hurt.)

lines.japanese: （誰かそばにいてやらないとダメなんだ）
lines.english: (Someone has to stay with her.)

lines.japanese: だけど、とためらいもする。
lines.english: But still, he hesitated.

lines.japanese: （友達なんていないのに）
lines.english: (I don't even have any friends.)

lines.japanese:
（……そんな人間なのに、うまくやっていけるのか
　な？）
lines.english: (...Can someone like me really get along with her?)

lines.japanese:
（傷つけたりしないかな。ぎこちなくなったり、し
　ないかな……？）

lines.english: “Know what?”

lines.japanese: 牽制のため、皮肉を言うことにした。
lines.english: He chose sarcasm to hold her at a distance.

lines.japanese: 「きみに関わると、ろくなことがないって」
lines.english: “Nothing good ever comes of getting involved with you.”
“What?!”

lines.japanese:
「前のときだって、助けたのにわるものにされるし
　……今回だって何があったのかと思ってさがせば
　……寝てるだけだし」
lines.english: “Last time, I helped you and you treated me like the bad guy ...and this time I came looking because I thought something had happened ...but you were only asleep.”

lines.japanese: 「こんなところで寝たらダメだ」
lines.english: “You shouldn't sleep in a place like this.”

lines.japanese:
「うるさいなー！
　どこで寝たってあたしのかってでしょー！」
lines.english: “Oh, shut up! I can sleep wherever I want!”

lines.japanese: 「服、泥だらけだよ、きみ」
lines.english: “Your clothes are covered in mud, you know.”
“Oh... crap...”

lines.japanese: 「まったく、もう」
lines.english: “Honestly.”

lines.japanese: 「うー、頭ベリベリする……」
lines.english: “Ugh, my head feels all crackly...”

lines.japanese: 「地べたに頭つけて寝るから」
lines.english: “Because you slept with your head on the ground.”

lines.japanese: 「だって……」
「怪我は？」
lines.english: “Are you hurt?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ないよ。だいじょうび」
lines.english: “Nope. I'm fime.”

lines.japanese: 「痛むところは？」
lines.english: “Does anything hurt?”

lines.japanese: 「ないって」
lines.english: “I said no.”

lines.japanese: 「……吐き気は？」
lines.english: “...Any nausea?”

lines.japanese: 「もー、ないってんだろー！　しっこい！」
lines.english: “I said no! Quit bugging me!”

lines.japanese: 「なら、いい」
lines.english: “Then that’s all right.”

lines.japanese: 忍は元来た道を戻る。
lines.english: Shinobu turned back the way he had come.

lines.japanese: 「あ、どうするの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Where are you going?”

lines.japanese: 「医者に行くよ。言い訳しないと」
lines.english: “To the doctor. I have to explain myself.”

lines.japanese:
「それと、滑った時に頭でもうったのなら一応、
　親御さんに話した方がいい」
lines.english: “And if you hit your head when you fell, you should probably tell your parents, just in case.”

lines.japanese: 「土だから、平気だと思うけど」
lines.english: “You landed on dirt, so I think you'll be all right.”

lines.japanese: 「滑ったんじゃないよぅ……」
lines.english: “I didn't slip...”
“—Bye.”

lines.japanese: なんとか事もなく終わった。
lines.english: Somehow, it ended without incident.

lines.japanese: 「ねー！」
lines.english: “Hey!”

lines.japanese: 呼びかけられ、振り返る。
lines.english: At her call, he turned.

lines.japanese: 「これって、助けられたってことー？」
lines.english: “So does this mean you saved me?”

lines.japanese:
少し驚く。
　助けた行為を、彼女が知っているはずもない。
lines.english: He was mildly surprised. She had no way of knowing what he had done to help her.

lines.japanese:
声をかけた程度のことで、感謝の念を抱かれても
困る。
lines.english: He did not want her feeling grateful merely because he had spoken to her.

lines.japanese: 近づかれては困る。
lines.english: He could not have her coming closer.
“...Who knows!”

lines.japanese: 突き放すように叫んだ。
lines.english: He shouted it to drive her away.

lines.japanese:
忍がまだ籠の中の鳥でしかなかった頃。
　少女は、彼に恋をした。
lines.english: Back when Shinobu was still nothing but a bird in a cage, a girl fell in love with him.

lines.japanese: 『いつも、何を見えますか？』
lines.english: “Always, what can be seen by you?”

lines.japanese: 『楽しいものですか？　美しいものですか？』
lines.english: “Is it a pleasant thing? Is it a beautiful thing?”

lines.japanese: 『私は美しいですか？』
lines.english: “Am I beautiful?”

lines.japanese:
『私は見えていますか？
　あなたの基準でそうですか？
　私のうちには興味があります』
lines.english: “Am I visible? Is it so by your standard? Inside me, there is interest.”

lines.japanese:
言葉もなく、忍は求愛に心をさらし続けた。
　痺れたように、動けなかった。
lines.english: Without a word, Shinobu kept his heart exposed to her courtship. Numb, he could not move.

lines.japanese:
思考が淵に沈みゆこうとするたび、甲高い声に叩
き起こされる。
lines.english: Each time his thoughts began to sink into the abyss, her shrill voice jolted him awake.

lines.japanese:
辟易とする声に忍の心はよりかたく閉ざされ……
　あとは、その繰り返しだった。
lines.english: The tiresome voice made Shinobu close his heart all the tighter… and then it would begin all over again.

lines.japanese:
『届いていますか？　届いていませんか？
　あなたは、私の恋人ですか？』
lines.english: “Is it reaching you? Is it not reaching you? Are you my lover?”

lines.japanese: そのとき忍は、事務的な殺意さえ抱いていた。
lines.english: At that moment, Shinobu even felt a businesslike urge to kill.

lines.japanese: 『ご返答を、ご返答を、ご返答を』
lines.english: “Your response. Your response. Your response.”

lines.japanese: 『……君の、名前は？』
lines.english: “…What's your name?”

lines.japanese:
『フランシスです。私はフランシスです。
　この美しい名前を、私は美しいと習いました。
　私は美しいものと認識し、愛しています』
lines.english: “I am Francis. I am Francis. I was taught that this beautiful name is beautiful. I recognize it as a beautiful thing, and I love it.”

lines.japanese: 『ＯＫ。フランシス。なら答えよう』
lines.english: “Okay, Francis. Then I'll answer you.”

lines.japanese:
まだ籠の中の鳥でしかなかった頃。
　忍はただ酷薄なだけの少年でしかなかった。
lines.english: Back when he was still nothing but a bird in a cage, Shinobu was still nothing but a cruel boy.

lines.japanese:
人間ならとてもできないことを、平気で行った。
　殺害と創造が等価値だった。
lines.english: Without hesitation, he did things no human being could have brought himself to do. Killing and creation held equal value.

lines.japanese:
指をひねられ苦痛に呻く子供を、心傷めることな
く見つめられた。
lines.english: He could watch a child groan in pain as their finger was twisted without feeling the slightest pang himself.

lines.japanese:
踏みつけることができた。
　抱き起こすことができた。
lines.english: He could trample the child. He could lift the child up.

lines.japanese:
引き裂くことも。
　撫でることも。
lines.english: He could tear the child apart. He could stroke the child.

lines.japanese:
そして何より、自分の痛みさえ知らなかった。
　忍はいろいろ試した。
lines.english: More than anything, he did not even know his own pain. Shinobu tried all sorts of things.

lines.japanese:
自由に動く体の限り、試した。
　物心というものがつき、認識力が格段に上昇した
が、性行に変化はなかった。
lines.english: He tried everything his freely moving body allowed. He acquired what people call self-awareness, and his powers of perception rose dramatically, but his conduct did not change.

lines.japanese: 冷たく残酷な幼子は、痛みを学ぶことはなかった。
lines.english: The cold, cruel child never learned pain.

lines.japanese: 少女はそれでも、忍に恋をした。
lines.english: Even so, the girl fell in love with Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 『ＯＫ。フランシス』
lines.english: “Okay, Francis.”

lines.japanese: 『なら答えよう』
lines.english: “Then I'll answer you.”

lines.japanese:
いまだ言葉のたどたどしい少女に、忍はいつもの
調子で告げる。
lines.english: The girl still stumbled over her words. Shinobu answered in his usual tone.

lines.japanese: 『僕は君が大嫌いだね』
lines.english: “I really do hate you.”

lines.japanese:
彼は断絶を創造してみた。
　理由はない。
lines.english: He tried creating a rift between them. There was no reason.

lines.japanese:
たまたま、そういうことを試してみたかったに過
ぎない。
lines.english: It simply happened to be something he felt like trying.

lines.japanese:
少女フランシスに対して、特別の気持ちがプラス
にしろマイナスにしろあったわけじゃない。
lines.english: He felt nothing special for the girl called Francis, positive or negative.

lines.japanese:
どちらでも良かった。
　たまたま、嫌いになってみた。
lines.english: Either would have suited him. On a whim, he tried hating her.

lines.japanese:
まったく興味がないということは、求愛する側に
とって拒絶という意味では大差ない。
lines.english: To the one doing the courting, complete indifference was little different from rejection.

lines.japanese:
フランシスは戸惑った。
　戸惑いが、伝わってきた。
lines.english: Francis was bewildered. Her bewilderment came through.

lines.japanese: 『嫌い？　嫌いなのですか？　なぜです？』
lines.english: “Hate? Do you hate me? Why?”

lines.japanese: 『嫌いだからさ』
lines.english: “Because I hate you.”

lines.japanese:
『わかりません。わかりません。嫌う理由を教えて
　ください』
lines.english: “I do not understand. I do not understand. Tell me your reason for hating me.”

lines.japanese: 『逆にきくけど』
lines.english: “Let me turn that question around.”

lines.japanese: 『なぜ好きなの？』
lines.english: “Why do you like me?”

lines.japanese:
『それを私はわかりません。私はそれを的確に説明
　できません可能性があります』
lines.english: “That, I do not understand. There is a possibility I cannot explain it accurately.”

lines.japanese: 『僕もわからない』
lines.english: “I don't know either.”

lines.japanese:
『私はあなたから多くを教わりたい。
　それは不可能ですか？』
lines.english: “I wish to learn many things from you. Is it impossible?”

lines.japanese: 『不可能だね』
lines.english: “It is.”

lines.japanese:
誠心誠意、嫌うことにした忍は、彼女に痛烈な言
葉ばかりを選んで浴びせかけた。
lines.english: In all sincerity, Shinobu had decided to hate her, and he chose only the most cutting words to hurl at her.

lines.japanese: 『二度とそのようなことを、僕に言わないでほしい』
lines.english: “I never want you to say anything like that to me again.”

lines.japanese: けたたましく語りかけてきた少女が、黙り込んだ。
lines.english: The girl who had spoken to him so shrilly fell silent.

lines.japanese:
途方もない戸惑いと混乱が伝わってきた。
　求愛もはじめてならば、拒絶もはじめて。
lines.english: An overwhelming sense of bewilderment and confusion came through. It was her first courtship, and her first rejection.

lines.japanese:
そして乙女にとって、異性による拒絶の言葉は毒
と認知される。
lines.english: And to a girl, rejection from a boy registers as poison.

lines.japanese: 舌に苦いばかりか、心を溶解させてしまうものだ。
lines.english: It tastes bitter on the tongue, then dissolves the heart.

lines.japanese: 沈黙となった。
lines.english: She went silent.

lines.japanese: 子供の数は、年々減っていった。
lines.english: The number of children dwindled with each passing year.

lines.japanese:
しかしその事実に忍が気付いたのは、人の減少が
だいぶん顕著になってからだ。
　もともと個人を判別する癖のなかった忍である。
　誰か特定の知り合いがいなくなれば、あるいはも
っと早くに気付くことができただろう。
lines.english: Shinobu did not notice until the decline in numbers had grown quite pronounced. He had never made a habit of distinguishing one person from another. Had a particular acquaintance vanished, he might have noticed sooner.

lines.japanese:
知り合いなどいなかった。
　名前さえほとんど、埒外の情報だったくらいだ。
　広いスペースを満たすほどいた同じ境遇の子供ら
が、半分になり、四分の一になって……ようやく少
ないな？と思い始めた。
lines.english: But he had no acquaintances. Even names were information that mostly lay outside his concerns. The children in circumstances like his, once numerous enough to fill the vast space, fell to half their number, then a quarter… Only then did he begin to think: There are fewer of us, aren't there?

lines.japanese:
確かに子供の数は多すぎた。
　大舎制の施設とはいえ、許容量を超えていた。
　決して広くはない部屋に５～８人が詰めこまれ、
共同生活を強いられた。
lines.english: There certainly had been too many children. Even by the standards of a dormitory-style facility, it was over capacity. Five to eight were crammed into rooms that were hardly spacious and forced to live together.

lines.japanese:
４月にはお花見。
　６月にはオリエンテーション。
　７月には七夕キャンプ。
lines.english: Cherry-blossom viewing in April. Orientation in June. A Tanabata camp in July.

lines.japanese:
月ごとにあったイベントも、管理色ばかりが強か
った。
　子供らにとってそれは、こなすべき義務でしかな
かったはずだ。
lines.english: Even the monthly events felt more administrative than recreational. To the children, they could only have been obligations to get through.

lines.japanese:
家庭的雰囲気などは存在しない。
　また児童らの誰も、求めていなかった。
lines.english: There was no family atmosphere. Nor did any of the children ask for one.

lines.japanese: 知らなかったからだ。
lines.english: They had never known one.

lines.japanese:
誰もが酷薄な性格を植え付けられた。
　狡猾さが肯定され、馬鹿正直な者が持つ人好きの
する部分は、徹底して淘汰・虚勢された。
lines.english: A hard heart was planted in every child. Cunning was rewarded. The qualities that made the guilelessly honest so likable were ruthlessly selected out and neutered.

lines.japanese:
大人は誰も、子供同士の政治に介入したりはしな
かった。
　才走った者が権勢をふるう。
　もっともシンプルな形での集団倫理。
lines.english: None of the adults ever intervened in the politics among the children. The quick-witted took power. Group ethics in its simplest form.

lines.japanese: 忍は一匹狼だった。
lines.english: Shinobu was a lone wolf.

lines.japanese: 徒党を組むということがない。
lines.english: He never ran with a pack.

lines.japanese:
それは忍が施設での倫理をもっとも深く学び取っ
た証であり、他の児童を区別できないほど徹底した
自己意識が形成されていたからだ。
　弱ければ、早々に虐待の餌食になっていたはずで
ある。
lines.english: It proved he had learned the facility's code more deeply than anyone else. His sense of self had become so complete that he could not even distinguish the other children. Had he been weak, he would quickly have become prey for their abuse.

lines.japanese: しかし忍は生存した。
lines.english: But Shinobu survived.

lines.japanese:
苦痛さえ解さない忍は、単体とはいえ危険な、利
害を鑑みない地雷のようなものだった。
　踏んだ者の足を、無差別に持っていく。
　誰も触れようとは思わない。
lines.english: Shinobu did not even comprehend pain. Alone, he was still dangerous— a land mine that paid no heed to gain or loss. Whoever stepped on him lost a foot. No one wanted to touch him.

lines.japanese:
児童が消えた件は、別にきな臭い話ではない。
　人生何があるかわからないのだから、中には死ん
だ者もいたかも知れないが、その多くは移動による。
　すし詰め状態だった宿舎から、各地の施設に。
　空間にもゆとりができ、設備もよく利用できるよ
うになる。
lines.english: There was nothing sinister about the children disappearing. You never knew what life might bring, so some might even have died, but most had simply been transferred. From the packed dormitory to facilities around the country. There was room to breathe now, and the amenities were easier to use.

lines.japanese: 噂が流れた。
lines.english: A rumor began to circulate.

lines.japanese:
ちょうど四分の一になった時、忍も耳にする。
　成績によって、区分けを行っている……というも
のだ。
lines.english: When only a quarter remained, the rumor reached Shinobu too. They were being sorted… according to their performance.

lines.japanese:
だとすれば、自分らが今いるこの場所は、どの程
度のランクに該当するのだうう？
　またそのことによって、将来どんな素晴らしい未
来が待っているのだろう？
　子供である以上、享楽主義的な面は否めない。
　確たる証左もなく、信じたいものを信じる無垢が、
そこにはあった。
lines.english: If so, what rank did the place they occupied now represent? And what marvelous future might that ranking have in store for them? They were children; a certain hedonistic streak was inevitable. They had the innocence to believe whatever they wished to believe, without a shred of proof.

lines.japanese: 忍にはなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu did not.

lines.japanese: どうでも良かった。
lines.english: He did not care.

lines.japanese:
彼も人並みに抜け道を使ってはいたが、一人で海
に行ってはそのまま帰るのみの日々。
　脱走しようなどとは、露ほども考えない。
lines.english: He too used the secret ways out, but only to go to the sea alone and then come straight back. Running away for good never once crossed his mind.

lines.japanese:
自活手段がなければ無意味だ。
　養護施設に対する不満もない。
　ただ海を見るだけだ。
lines.english: Without a way to support himself, there was no point. He had no complaints about the facility. He went only to look at the sea.

lines.japanese:
忍のイメージにおいて、海は巨大な脳だった。
　脳が頭蓋のうちで、脊髄液に浸かっている……と
いうことを知ったからだ。
　有機的に繋がった海には、無数のプランクトンが
存在している。
lines.english: In Shinobu's imagination, the sea was an enormous brain. He had learned that the brain floated inside the skull, immersed in cerebrospinal fluid. And the sea, connected into an organic whole, contained countless plankton.

lines.japanese: その二つが重なる。
lines.english: The two images overlapped.

lines.japanese:
なぜ重なるのか、なぜ気になるのか……忍は自己
のうちに言及しない。
lines.english: Why the images overlapped, why they interested him… Shinobu never looked within himself for an answer.

lines.japanese:
黙して受け入れた。
　言葉なく感じ続けた。
lines.english: He accepted it in silence. He went on feeling it without words.

lines.japanese: 児童数は八分の一。
lines.english: The children dwindled to one-eighth their original number.

lines.japanese:
正月には外部から、芸人が呼ばれた。
　奮発したものである。
　まったく笑わないか、笑ってもどこか異質な子供
らを、彼らはどう思ったのだろうか？
lines.english: At New Year's, entertainers were brought in from outside. A lavish gesture. What did they make of children who either never laughed, or whose laughter, when it came, seemed somehow alien?

lines.japanese:
残された児童は、スペックが高い子供らのようだ
った。
lines.english: The children who remained seemed to be the high-spec ones.

lines.japanese: 忍はそう感じた。
lines.english: That was Shinobu's impression.

lines.japanese: そして事実でもある。
lines.english: It was also true.

lines.japanese:
この期に及んで、彼はまだ外界を曖昧に見ていた
が、印象深い出来事のいくつかを特別に記憶するよ
うになった。
lines.english: Even at this stage, he still saw the outside world only dimly, but a handful of striking events began to earn a special place in his memory.

lines.japanese:
感性の領域だけが告げる、特別の“色”を見分け
るように。
lines.english: He began to distinguish the special “colors” that only his sensibilities could perceive.

lines.japanese: ある夜、脱出現場を発見された。
lines.english: One night, he was caught sneaking out.

lines.japanese: 「……おい、おまえ、逃げるのか？」
lines.english: “…Hey. Are you running away?”

lines.japanese: 「海を見る」
lines.english: “I'm going to see the sea.”

lines.japanese: 「見てどうする」
lines.english: “What will you do there?”

lines.japanese: 「見るだけだよ」
lines.english: “Just look.”

lines.japanese: 「……戻ってくるのか？」
lines.english: “…Are you coming back?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん……」
lines.english: “Huh…”

lines.japanese: 少年は物珍しそうに、忍を眺めた。
lines.english: The boy studied Shinobu with open curiosity.

lines.japanese: 「告げ口したければそうすればいいよ」
lines.english: “You can tell on me if you want.”

lines.japanese: 「別に……そういうことをしたいわけじゃない」
lines.english: “No… It's not like I want to.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえと話すのは、はじめてだな」
lines.english: “First time I've talked to you.”

lines.japanese: 「……誰だっけ？」
lines.english: “…Who were you again?”

lines.japanese: 少年は面食らったようだった。
lines.english: The boy looked taken aback.

lines.japanese: 「……そういう手合いか、おまえは」
lines.english: “…Oh. So that's the kind of person you are.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いい……」
lines.english: “Nah, forget it…”

lines.japanese: 「まあ戻るならいいさ。戻らなくとも……」
lines.english: “Well, if you're coming back, fine. Even if you don't…”

lines.japanese: 「ライバルが一人減るだけだしな」
lines.english: “It just means one less rival for me.”

lines.japanese: 「……よくわからないな」
lines.english: “…I don't get it.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことも言ってられなくなる。そのうち」
lines.english: “You won't be able to say that much longer.”

lines.japanese: 「俺たちみたいな国の子はさ」
lines.english: “Kids who belong to the state, like us—”

lines.japanese: 「誰の子供だってかまわないよ」
lines.english: “I don't care whose kid I am.”

lines.japanese:
「行っていいかな。巡回時間までにはベッドに戻り
　たいんだ」
lines.english: “Can I go now? I want to be back in bed before their rounds.”

lines.japanese:
少年は腕を組んで考え込んでいた。
　反応がなかったので、忍はそのまま立ち去ろうと
した。
lines.english: The boy folded his arms and sank into thought. When no answer came, Shinobu turned to leave.

lines.japanese: 背中に、少年の声が弱々しく当たった。
lines.english: The boy's voice fell weakly against his back.

lines.japanese:
「どうせ逃げられやしないんだ……
　おまえも、おれも」
lines.english: “There's no getting away, anyway… Not for you. Not for me.”

lines.japanese: 他者―――
lines.english: Others—

lines.japanese:
異質なもの。
　理解できないもの。
　相容れないもの。
　外部存在。
lines.english: Something alien. Something impossible to understand. Something incompatible. An external entity.

lines.japanese:
いつ頃からか忍も“他者”なるものを意識しはじめ
た。
lines.english: At some point, Shinobu too began to recognize the existence of others.

lines.japanese:
見渡せば、周囲にはいくらでも人間はいた。
　細密に観察していくと、多くの情報が取り込める。
　風貌。
　言動。
　思想。
　策謀。
　癖。
　臭い。
　強さ。
lines.english: All he had to do was look around: there were people everywhere. Close observation yielded a wealth of information. Appearance. Speech and behavior. Ideas. Schemes. Habits. Smell. Strength.

lines.japanese:
構築された人間関係の相関図を、そらで書ける程度
に読解が進むと、次は気になる者とそうでない者の差
を考えてみた。
　論理的な回答は自らの内にはなく、抽象的な分類に
頼らざるを得なかった。
lines.english: Once he had studied them well enough to draw the entire map of their relationships from memory, he turned to the difference between those who interested him and those who did not. He found no logical answer within himself. He had no choice but to rely on abstract categories.

lines.japanese:
彼らを、忍は“濃密な者”と認識していた。
　通常の人間に比べて強い存在感を発している者たち
だ。
lines.english: Shinobu thought of them as “the intense ones.” They radiated a stronger presence than ordinary people.

lines.japanese:
傾向によって、種々様々なタイプがいた。
　彼らは忍の目に、怪物にしか見えなかった。
　巨大な可能性を秘めた者が、そうでない者たちの
隙間に何食わぬ顔で生きている。
　忍の脳は、彼らに対し警戒を発し続けた。
lines.english: There were all sorts, each with its own tendencies. To Shinobu, they could only look like monsters. People harboring immense potential lived among those who did not, wearing an air of perfect unconcern. Shinobu's brain kept sounding the alarm.

lines.japanese:
何に対する警戒なのか、そしてどのような実行力を
“怪物”たちが持つのか、まるで見当もつかない。
　成熟した精神ならば、『今のうちになんとかしなけ
ればならない』という結論に至ったかもしれない。
　端的には、殺傷能力などに直結するだろう。
lines.english: He had no idea what the warning was for, or what capacity for action those monsters might possess. A more mature mind might have concluded that something had to be done about them while there was still time. In the simplest terms, that led directly to the capacity to kill or maim.

lines.japanese:
優れた人間は、同種を制する術に長けているはずで
ある。
　でなければ競走を生き延びることはできない。
　もっともストレートな手段は暴力だ。
　そして倫理を踏み越える、非人間的ともいえる決断
力。
lines.english: A superior human being ought to excel at controlling others of the same species. Otherwise they could not survive the competition. Violence was the most direct means. Beyond it lay the inhuman decisiveness to step across the line of ethics.

lines.japanese:
ないしは必要と判断した瞬間に実行できる能力。
　筋力等、後天的に備わるものはさして恐ろしく
ない。
　選りすぐりの肉質であるなら話は別だが、人間と怪
物をわかつのは脳力差である。
　社会は凡人にあわせて作られている。
　だから怪物らはそこにはマッチしないことが多い。
lines.english: Or the ability to act the instant action was judged necessary. Things acquired later, such as physical strength, were not especially frightening. An exceptional physical constitution might be another matter, but what divided human from monster was a difference in brainpower. Society was built to suit ordinary people. The monsters often failed to fit within it.

lines.japanese: 世界は怪物たちを生み出しつつあった―――
lines.english: The world was bringing monsters into being—

lines.japanese:
忍が自分のいる施設に疑問を感じたのも、
この頃になる。
lines.english: It was around then that Shinobu began to question the facility where he lived.

lines.japanese:
職員が、とある少女に時計を見せている。
　遊びのようにして見せている。
lines.english: A staff member was showing a girl a clock. Making a game of it.

lines.japanese:
無数の時計が床に並べられた。とりどりに。
　もっとも好ましいものを選ばせて、手に取らせる。
lines.english: Countless clocks of every kind were arrayed across the floor. They made her choose the one she liked best and pick it up.

lines.japanese:
気に入った順番に並べ替えさせたり、二つのグル
ープに振り分けさせたりする。
lines.english: They had her arrange them in order of preference, or sort them into two groups.

lines.japanese:
忍の知る限り、こういった個別の遊びは、施設内
では日常的に行われている。
lines.english: As far as Shinobu knew, these individual play sessions were an everyday occurrence at the facility.

lines.japanese:
誘われる者とそうでない者がいて、忍はまだ一度
も声をかけられたことはない。
lines.english: Some children were invited and others were not. No one had ever invited Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
嫌われているのかもしれない、という考え方さえ
育っていない、幼い日。
lines.english: He was so young then that the thought they might dislike him had yet to take shape.

lines.japanese:
ありのままを受け入れて、疑問ひとつなかった。
　件の少女の名前は調べたこともないし、容貌につ
いてもさして興味はなかった。
lines.english: He accepted things exactly as they were and never questioned them. He had never tried to learn the girl's name, nor did her appearance particularly interest him.

lines.japanese:
彼女は分類上は“ちょっとだけ怖い”程度の存在
で、注目するには値しない。
lines.english: By his classification, she was merely “a little frightening”—not enough to merit attention.

lines.japanese:
ただ継続して、時計をモチーフにした遊びを繰り
返し繰り返し受けさせられていたことは、記憶に残
っている。
lines.english: But he remembered how they kept putting her through the same games built around clocks and watches, over and over again.

lines.japanese:
なぜならそれは……少女を変えてしまうプログラ
ムだとわかったからだ。
lines.english: Because he realized… it was a program designed to change the girl.

lines.japanese: 見るからに。
lines.english: Plainly enough.

lines.japanese:
週に一度の時があった。
　日に三度の時もあった。
lines.english: Sometimes it happened once a week. Sometimes three times a day.

lines.japanese:
法則は不明だが、継続して綴られたことは間違い
ない。
lines.english: He could see no pattern, but there was no question the process had continued to be written into her.

lines.japanese: それ以外のことはろくに教育されなかった―――
lines.english: She received scarcely any other education—

lines.japanese:
そしてある日。
　少女の発する声を、忍は聞いた。
lines.english: Then one day. Shinobu heard the girl's voice.

lines.japanese: 廊下ですれ違った時だった。
lines.english: They were passing each other in the hall.

lines.japanese: 「……ちっくたっくちっくたっくちっくたっく……」
lines.english: “…tick-tock tick-tock tick-tock…”

lines.japanese: 歩きながら時計の擬した音を口にする。
lines.english: She imitated the sound of a clock as she walked.

lines.japanese:
子供の悪ふざけでしかない。
　だが断じて子供の悪ふざけではない。
lines.english: Nothing but a child's prank. Yet absolutely not a child's prank.

lines.japanese:
それは機能。
　後天的に付与された。
　改良されたのだ。
lines.english: It was a function. Something installed after the fact. She had been improved.

lines.japanese:
教育とも言うかもしれない。
　人は人を改良する。
　いろいろなツールを用いる。
lines.english: Some might call it education. People improve other people. They use any number of tools.

lines.japanese:
怒声・体罰・ルール・決まり・優しさ・ぬくもり・
食物・玩具……倫理―――
lines.english: Shouting, corporal punishment, rules, regulations, kindness, warmth, food, toys… ethics—

lines.japanese:
放置された赤子はせいぜい獣にしかならない。
　人はその設計思想に、改良を含んだ命だ。
　少女がされたことがまさにそうなのだ！
lines.english: An infant left to itself will become, at best, an animal. The very design of human life includes improvement. That was precisely what had been done to this girl!

lines.japanese: 慄然として、忍は背筋を伸ばした。
lines.english: Shinobu shuddered and drew himself upright.

lines.japanese:
大勢の人間が会話しているパーティー会場などでも、自分に関する会話だけは
不思議と耳に入るものである。この現象をカクテルパーティー効果と呼ぶ。
lines.english: Even at a crowded party where many people are talking at once, conversations about us have a curious way of finding our ears. This phenomenon is known as the cocktail-party effect.

lines.japanese:
なぜこのようなことが起こるのか。
　それは人間の耳の機能、そして認識のシステム、二つの面からのアプローチに
よって理解できる。
　まずハードウェアとしての人間は、二箇所のマイク……耳を持つ。
　二箇所の耳は同じ箇所にはなく、左右の一対である。
lines.english: What makes this possible? We can approach the question from two directions: how the human ear functions and how recognition works. At the hardware level, a human being comes equipped with two microphones… the ears. They do not occupy the same point, but form a pair on the left and right.

lines.japanese:
そのため両耳に届く音波の時間差により、音源との距離感をはかることができ
る。これに音声周波数の変化に乏しい特性をあわせ、周囲のどのあたりでどのよ
うな波長の音が流れているか空間認識的に把握することが可能である。
　さらにそれら混線する会話に対して、注意を払っていないようで、意識下では
ある程度自動的に処理されている。
lines.english: The difference in arrival time between the sound waves reaching either ear therefore lets us gauge our distance from the source. Speech also tends not to vary greatly in frequency. Taken together, these properties allow us to map where around us sounds of different wavelengths are being produced. Moreover, even when we seem to pay no attention to the overlapping conversations, some processing occurs automatically below the threshold of consciousness.

lines.japanese:
認知の度合いは高く、単に物理的特性による区別ではない。
　それぞれの会話内容に対して意味的に判別される。
　心理上の検索機能は常時働いており、自らの興味とリンクすることで、蓄積さ
れた会話からの抽出は極めて素早く実行されるのである。
lines.english: Recognition goes far beyond distinctions based on physical properties alone. Each conversation is sorted by meaning as well. The mind’s search function never switches off: it matches what we hear against our own interests and retrieves relevant material from the accumulated conversation with remarkable speed.

lines.japanese:
生物は、己の知らない領域で常に周囲から情報を集めている。
　周囲からの情報がなければ生体として成立することはできない。
　どの動物でも同様の特性はあるが、それは生存に必要であるという側面が強い
がため、各機能は合理的なものとなる。
lines.english: Living creatures constantly gather information from their surroundings outside their conscious awareness. Without external information, no organism could sustain itself as a living entity. Every animal has similar faculties. Because they exist primarily to ensure survival, each is rationally structured.

lines.japanese:
しかし人間はどうだろう。
　人は生まれてからは育つため、育ってからは生きるため、生きてからは何かの
ために情報を摂取し続ける。
lines.english: But what of humanity? From birth, we take in information so that we may grow; once grown, so that we may live; once living, for the sake of something else.

lines.japanese: 情報を。
lines.english: Information.

lines.japanese: より高精度な情報を。
lines.english: Information of ever greater precision.

lines.japanese:
やがて人は自らの五感だけでは飽き足らず、感覚器の拡張を行ってきた。
　そして今、人は溢れるほどの情報に囲まれている。
　しかし時として、一様な価値観が形成されることが多いのはなぜだろう。
　選択は無数にあり得るのに、同期が起こりやすいのはなぜだろう。
　簡単には、結論は出ない。
lines.english: In time, our five senses were no longer enough, and we began extending our sensory organs. Today, information surrounds us to overflowing. Yet why do people so often converge on a single system of values? With countless choices possible, why do we synchronize so readily? There is no simple answer.

lines.japanese:
もし外部からの情報が途絶した時、高度に発達したとされる人の意識は、どの
ような状態に置かれるのだろう。
lines.english: If the flow of information from the outside were severed, what state would the supposedly highly developed human consciousness be left in?

lines.japanese:
外に出るのか、あるいは内に向かうのか。
　心地よい自室は、いつも間口を広くして宿主を待っている。
lines.english: Would it emerge into the outside world, or turn inward? One's comfortable room is always waiting for its host, its entrance flung wide.

lines.japanese: 人の心と自室は、同じ広さと限度を共有することが多いのかも知れない。
lines.english: Perhaps the human heart and the room it calls its own often share the same dimensions—and the same limits.

lines.japanese: 自衛隊の最高責任者は内閣総理大臣である。
lines.english: Ultimate responsibility for the Japan Self-Defense Forces rests with the Prime Minister.

　あずさ→（すき！）→沙也加
　あずさ→（あったまいー、超おぱい、メガネ取ると美人なのだ）→笛子

　あずさ→（お父さんって感じ、
　　　　　　みんなに内緒でいろいろ買ってもらってる）→斎
